mail.title: The valley's forgotten stories
mail.welcome: Dear explorer,^The valley's soil holds many stories. I have prepared a field journal and notes on your first dig sites.^Press O for your journal and K to survey. Shortcuts can be changed in config.json. You can collect a journal and instrument from the first page.^Bring restored artifacts to the museum and register them in our separate research archive through the journal.^I look forward to your discoveries!^^   - Gunther

journal.title: Archaeology · Secrets of the Valley
journal.guide:
1. Choose a site on the opposite page.

2. Press {{survey}} at the location. Follow the arrow and signal colour.

3. Survey again when close. Dig the golden tile with your hoe.

4. Open a culture tab to restore artifacts from fragments.

Journal shortcut: {{journal}}.
journal.no-sites: All available sites are complete. New notes arrive in the morning.

workshop.title: Workshop Under the Mountain
workshop.case.name: Archaeology Display Case
workshop.ready: All parts recovered! Repair the digger back on your farm.
workshop.requirements: Check the requirements on the current story page.
workshop.case-crafted: Display case ready! Place it and put a find on top.
workshop.companion-on: The clockwork digger joins your expedition!
workshop.companion-off: The digger is resting. Call it back through the journal.

workshop.step.4: The first turn of a key
workshop.heading.0: A story waiting to be found
workshop.text.0:
A small workshop once operated beneath the mountain. Its owner made helpers for curious travellers.

Begin with dwarven dig sites: your first find in that field will uncover a lead.
workshop.text.1:
An oiled sheet survived between layers of soil. It shows a tiny mechanical animal, with a note: 'Dig with curiosity.'

Bring your notes to the museum. Speak to Gunther at the counter, or use the button in this book while inside the museum.
workshop.text.2:
Gunther found a similar drawing in an old inventory. The machine was called a digger: it sensed traces of objects shaped by working hands.

Show Robin the blueprint. Talk to her, or open this page while standing close to her.
workshop.text.3:
Robin marked three missing components. They cost no research fragments. After speaking with her, each suitable find guarantees a missing part.

Spring: dwarven finds.
Lens: coastal finds.
Core: valley heritage finds.

Ordinary worm spots also qualify when their bonus fragment drops are enabled.
workshop.text.4:
The spring is wound, the lens is clean, and the core glows softly. Only the housing and final assembly remain.

Return to the farm or your farmhouse with 20 wood and 5 copper bars. Make room for your reward display case.
workshop.text.5:
The digger's belly reads 'Dig with curiosity.' It follows your footsteps and turns its nose toward nearby antiquities. In the evening at home, it starts to doze.

Your first case is in your backpack. Place it indoors or on the farm, and put a regular artifact on it as you would on a table.

Call or dismiss your companion here, or build additional cases.
workshop.dialogue.gunther:
Gunther carefully smooths out the blueprint.

'I've seen this drawing in an old workshop inventory. It says: a helper for those who notice the past. Robin should know how to bring it back to life.'

A copy of the record is added to your journal. Next: show the blueprint to Robin.
workshop.dialogue.robin:
Robin turns the sheet, estimating dimensions.

'What a lovely design! I can work out the housing. But you'll need a winding spring, a clear lens, and this strange core. The drawing marks three different places. Its maker must have collected parts all over the valley.'

Three notes are added to the journal: mountains, coast, and old settlements.
workshop.dialogue.complete:
First, one click. Then another. Brass paws cautiously touch the floor.

The digger sneezes a cloud of old dust and nudges your hand. Its first discovery is you.

Workshop Under the Mountain is complete! Your digger will accompany you, and your first display case is in your backpack.
weather.title: Traces of the Weather
weather.guide:
The morning after a rainy day may reveal an old encampment. After a thunderstorm, charred roots can expose an underhill mechanism.

A special site contains 3 finds and lasts {{days}} days. Your instrument prioritizes it before ordinary digs.

The first completion of each type grants a new relic. Repeats give extra fragments and a keystone.

At least {{cooldown}} days separate new sites. Unfinished sites remain until their expiry. Unclaimed rewards wait in the journal indefinitely.
weather.disabled: New weather sites are disabled in config.json. Existing sites can still be completed.
weather.lead: The lead '{{name}}' is waiting for a safe map position. Days remaining: {{days}}.

weather.artifact-hint.storm: This relic lies beneath charred roots. Check the Weather tab the morning after a storm and excavate all three finds. Ordinary research fragments are not needed.

shipwreck.title: Letters from the Sunken Schooner
shipwreck.discovered: Three stars on a buckle… A sunken schooner story has opened in your journal!
shipwreck.heading.1: Three stars without a return date
shipwreck.heading.6: The voice of the Three Stars
shipwreck.text.0: Restore the Sunken Schooner Buckle in the sea culture. Its mark is your first lead. If you have already restored it, the story opens automatically when you load your save, even if you donated or sold the item.
shipwreck.text.1: Three stars have emerged on the buckle. Visit the museum, open this page inside the building and study the harbour records with Gunther. You do not need to hand over the buckle.
shipwreck.text.2: Gunther found the schooner Three Stars. She disappeared off the valley's coast, yet no losses were recorded. A knot is drawn in the margin. Approach Willy and ask him about it; the button below works near the fisherman wherever he is.
shipwreck.text.3: Willy recognises his old mentor's knot, used to seal letters in bottles. Play a rainy or stormy day, then survey the western beach the following morning. The bottle can be found for three days after rain. If you miss it, another rainy day gives you a new chance. This story works even when ordinary weather expeditions are disabled.
shipwreck.text.4: A sealed bottle lay beneath the sand. The paper survived; you can reread the letter in your journal. It mentions 'quiet water beyond the old landing'. Approach Willy to understand the captain's words.
shipwreck.text.5: Willy explained that the captain meant the old landing on the western beach. Survey that shore and excavate three finds in the final cache. Take your time: there is no deadline, and you do not need to repair the tide-pool bridge.
shipwreck.text.6: A ship's bell emerged from the sand, wrapped in an old sail. A note beside it reads: 'Everyone made it ashore. May it call us home again someday.' The bell will wait in your journal until you have backpack space.
shipwreck.text.7: The Three Stars never logged her return: the sailors went home on foot, leaving the damaged ship to the sea. Her bell can sing on dry land again. Place it at home or on the farm and press the action button to restore 35 energy once per day. All copies share one charge per player; full energy preserves it. The letter remains in the journal archive.
shipwreck.dialogue.gunther: Gunther traces an old entry with his finger.^The Three Stars. Departure date, cargo… but no return entry. Yet not a single name among the lost.^See this knot in the margin? I've copied it into your journal. Ask Willy. He knows sea signs better than my dusty shelves.
shipwreck.dialogue.willy: Willy studies the sketch for a long time.^My old mentor used that knot to seal letters for the folks waiting ashore. A sturdy binding. That bottle could have spent years in the sand.^Rain washes the top layer away. Check the western beach the next morning, friend. Your instrument ought to pick it up.
shipwreck.dialogue.decode: Willy smooths out a copy of the letter.^'Quiet water'… Old sailors called the place by the western landing that. Not across the bridge. Right beside the road home.^They took the bell off before she sank. They must have reached the shore. Find that cache, friend. Give this story its voice back.
shipwreck.letter:
Dear Mara,

If this bottle reaches you before we do, don't believe the rumours about the ship. Everyone is ashore. Even our grumpy cook.

We took the bell down before the water reached the deck and hid it where the sea grows quiet beyond the old landing. Three marks in the sand will show the place.

The schooner will stay here. We will walk home. Perhaps this time I won't smell of fresh fish, though I make no promises.

Yours, Elias.
Captain of the Three Stars.

On the back, in another hand: 'Everyone made it. May it call us home again someday.'
shipwreck.requirements: This step requires the museum or Willy nearby. Check the current objective in your journal.
shipwreck.archive: Recovered letters stay in your journal.

shipwreck.active-cache: Beach finds remaining: {{count}}. Survey with {{key}}, then dig the highlighted tiles with your hoe. There is no deadline.

shipwreck.cache-found: The schooner's cache is complete! A ship's bell awaits in your journal.
shipwreck.reward-received: The bell of the Three Stars is yours!
shipwreck.bell-description: A bell from the sunken schooner. Place it and press the action button: +35 energy once a day. All copies share one charge per player; full energy preserves it.
shipwreck.bell-used: The bell has already helped you today. Its voice will return in the morning.

nature.title: Traces of natural events
nature.discovered: New dig: {{name}} · {{location}}. See the journal's Nature tab.
nature.completed: {{name}}: +{{fragments}} fragments, {{experience}} experience and the site keystone!
nature.reward-waiting: A new find awaits in the journal's Nature tab. Make room and claim it.
nature.waiting: Waiting for a new natural event.
nature.tomorrow: This lead opens the next morning.
nature.queued: This lead awaits free, accessible ground. Days remaining: {{days}}. Its original deadline is unchanged.
nature.guide.snow: The first observed snowy day of each year leaves a lead for the next morning. Three finds appear in the forest, backwoods or town for {{days}} days. Installing on a snowy day also counts as the first observation.
nature.guide.season: The first day of a new season opens three beach finds for {{days}} days. The mod must observe the season change; installing on the first day does not create a retroactive event.
nature.guide.meteor: A new farm meteorite opens three finds within 8 tiles of the impact for {{days}} days. Meteorites present at the first observation are ignored. You do not need to break the rock. If the ground is occupied, clear ordinary soil and reload before the lead expires.
nature.rules: The first completion of each kind gives a unique artifact, stored in the journal until claimed. Repeat sites grant fragments, experience and a keystone. Snow and shore: +12 fragments and 45 experience; meteor: +18 and 75. All three kinds can coexist. Finds avoid water, crops and buildings. The hourglass can extend a site once.
nature.disabled: New sites are disabled. Observations continue; existing sites and rewards remain available until their own deadlines. Events during disabled days do not accumulate.
nature.artifact-hint.snow: Snow covered something forgotten. Finish Beneath the First Snow; its lead opens the morning after the year's first observed snowy day.
nature.artifact-hint.season: More than the weather changes on the shore. Finish Shore of a New Season after a season change.
nature.artifact-hint.meteor: A fallen star left traces in the farm's soil. Finish the dig beside a new meteorite.
residents.title: Every object has a voice
residents.discovered: A find has a personal story. {{name}} can help; see the journal's Residents tab.
residents.site-found: {{name}}: a new cache at {{location}}. Two finds, no deadline.
residents.shared: Story shared with {{name}}. +{{friendship}} friendship, {{experience}} experience. A relic awaits in the journal.
residents.requirements: Approach the resident within 4 tiles and open Residents to talk. Sleeping residents and ongoing events are unavailable.
residents.no-space: No safe room for two finds yet. Clear ground at the destination and return next morning or reload. This lead will not expire.
residents.active: Cache: {{location}}. Finds remaining: {{count}}. Survey with {{key}}, then hoe the highlighted tiles. No deadline.
residents.reward: Keepsake: {{artifact}}. Cache bonus: {{fragments}} fragments; final conversation: {{friendship}} friendship and {{experience}} experience. The relic waits for backpack space in the journal and can be claimed once.
residents.stage.0: First restore the {{artifact}}. Its story opens automatically, even if you later sell, display or donate the find. Earlier discoveries count too.
residents.stage.1: {{name}} may recognise a mark on this find. Approach the resident, open this page and show your notes. You do not need to carry or hand over the object.
residents.stage.2: The first interpretation is archived. Survey {{location}} and recover two pieces of the story. Notes stay in the journal without using backpack space.
residents.stage.3: Both pieces recovered. {{name}} is waiting to hear the story: approach and discuss the notes using the button below. Your findings stay in the journal archive.
residents.stage.4: Story shared; friendship and experience already awarded. Claim the keepsake when you have backpack space. No further conversation is required to collect it.
residents.stage.5: Story complete. Conversations and the recovered note remain in this page's archive. The keepsake appears in its culture's collection.
residents.goal.penny: Penny recognises familiar attempts to fix a mistake on the apprentice's tablet. Her lead points to the town's paths.
residents.goal.evelyn: The swallow brooch reminds Evelyn of a springtime promise. Her lead follows forest paths to an old garden's traces.
residents.goal.willy: The sailor's clay whistle holds a simple signal from shore. Willy can help find its continuation on the western beach without repairing the bridge.
residents.artifact-hint.penny: Restore the Apprentice Runecarver's Tablet and follow Penny's story in the Residents tab.
residents.artifact-hint.evelyn: Restore the Copper Swallow Brooch and follow Evelyn's story in the Residents tab.
residents.artifact-hint.willy: Restore the Sailor's Clay Whistle and follow Willy's story in the Residents tab.
residents.dialogue.penny.start: May I see your notes? Runes aren't my specialty... but I recognise these repetitions. A pupil tries to write a symbol, gets frustrated, and rubs everything out.#$b#I might skip the bit about the teacher's moustache when reading to the children. Though Vincent would probably love it.#$b#Between the lines there's a path and two flat stones. It looks like the old town paths. Try your instrument there. Perhaps the rest of the lesson survived?
residents.dialogue.penny.share: The first tablet has the same symbol carved seven times. The second says... 'Once more. Better already.' So the teacher was patient after all.#$b#I'll keep a copy for our lessons. Sometimes a child needs to see that even an ancient teacher allowed mistakes.#$b#Take this seal. We can put it beside little discoveries. For paying attention, rather than getting the answer right.
residents.note.penny: Two practice tablets. Seven uneven symbols cover the first; the teacher wrote 'Once more. Better already.' on the second. A small moustache in the margin has been carefully framed.
residents.dialogue.evelyn.start: Oh, that little swallow... People gave those brooches with a promise to return in spring. I remember waiting for the birds by the road with my friend.#$b#We had a tiny garden beyond the forest path. We hid tin notes there about what we'd plant next year, like very grown-up gardeners.#$b#Perhaps the soil kept one. Try your instrument along the forest paths. Take your time. A good story, like a garden, knows how to wait.
residents.dialogue.evelyn.share: 'We'll plant more in spring. Even if they don't all grow.' My goodness... I'd forgotten those words, yet I kept living by them.#$b#There weren't any rare flowers. Just two girls, a handful of seeds and a very serious promise to meet again in spring. It was enough.#$b#I put a petal from my garden today in this locket. Take it. When you're tired, remember: you can start a new garden at any age.
residents.note.evelyn: Two tin covers show a child's drawing of a swallow and a garden. A paper inside reads: 'We'll plant more in spring. Even if they don't all grow.' The names faded; the promise survived.
residents.dialogue.willy.start: A little fish whistle? Ha! A proper shore thing. You'd use it to call a boat when your voice was lost in the wind, though never in a storm.#$b#Two short notes, one long. My father answered that way when I waited for his catch. I always whistled too early, then went red as a lobster.#$b#They left signal notes near the old paths on the western beach. Try your instrument there. You won't need the bridge to the pools.
residents.dialogue.willy.share: There's the note. 'Don't whistle until you see the sail.' Good advice... wish someone had told me.#$b#The other side says: 'If you're waiting, let them know you're here.' That one's more important. Someone in a boat is glad to hear a familiar sound too.#$b#I cleaned an old brass whistle for you. Two short notes, one long. May it guide you to the things waiting in the soil.
residents.note.willy: Pieces of a shore signal guide show a boat and a fish. One side reads 'Don't whistle until you see the sail.' The other: 'If you're waiting, let them know you're here.' Nothing about treasure; only coming home.
field.title: Objectives
field.empty: No active objectives right now. New digs are checked in the morning. The guide on the right can help you begin.
field.guide-notes:
The list combines all dig types, unclaimed rewards, story conversations and projects with enough fragments. Rewards come first, then digs with the nearest deadline. Use the page buttons or Up/Down arrows to browse longer lists.

Select an objective and open its page. You can pin one objective on screen. A pinned lead follows its newly placed excavation. Completed or expired objectives are unpinned automatically; other objectives stay in the journal.
field.navigation: Open the objective's page for details and available actions. If restoration needs a keystone, its toggle will be enabled. Review the cost before restoring.
field.tracked: Objective pinned. Its progress is shown on screen and saved in the journal.
field.untracked: Objective unpinned. It stays in the journal.
field.hidden-tracker: The objective is saved, but ShowHud or ShowTrackedObjective is hiding its panel.
field.location-unknown: Check the resident's schedule for their location
field.status.reward: A reward awaits in the journal
field.status.disabled: New sites of this kind are disabled
field.detail.reward: You have earned the {{artifact}}. Open its page and claim it when you have backpack space. Unclaimed rewards never expire.
field.detail.collection: Collection complete. Open the Gallery tab to claim the {{artifact}} furniture reward. It waits for backpack space and can be claimed once.
field.detail.dig:
Location: {{location}}. Finds remaining: {{count}}. Days left, including today: {{days}}.

Use {{key}} near the dig. When the instrument highlights an exact tile, approach and dig it with your hoe. Other stories and digs continue independently.
field.detail.permanent-dig:
Location: {{location}}. Story finds remaining: {{count}}. There is no deadline; you can return another day.

Use {{key}}, follow the signal and hoe the highlighted tile.
field.detail.restore: You have enough fragments for the {{artifact}} project. Cost: {{cost}}. Open its page, make backpack space and restore the find.
field.detail.restore-key: You can restore the {{artifact}} using one keystone: {{cost}} fragments and one keystone. The project's keystone toggle will be enabled. Review the price and restore it when ready.
field.detail.part: The workshop still needs the {{part}}. Your next mod find in {{culture}} will guarantee it. Ordinary and special mod digs both count; the component stays in the journal.
field.detail.repair: All three components are ready. Return home or to the farm with {{wood}} wood and {{copper}} copper bars, then open the workshop and assemble the mole. Leave a backpack slot for the reward.
field.detail.tomorrow: This lead is recorded and opens the next morning. Its destination and original deadline are saved in the journal; reloading does not change them.
field.detail.queued: The lead is recorded, but its site has not been placed yet. All finds need free, walkable ground. Placement is retried next morning or on loading after space is cleared. See the research page for details and the original deadline.
field.detail.disabled: The lead is recorded, but new sites of this kind are disabled in settings. Its original deadline still runs. Open sites and unclaimed rewards remain available.
artifact.settler_cup.name: Settler's Cup
artifact.settler_cup.description: Display on a table or donate to the research archive.
artifact.settler_cup.lore: Scratched into the base: 'Tea still smells like home, even here.' Gunther believes this cup predates the valley's railway.
artifact.copper_brooch.name: Copper Swallow Brooch
artifact.copper_brooch.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.copper_brooch.lore: People exchanged these brooches as a promise to return in spring. One wing has been polished smooth by a thumb.
artifact.keeper_lantern.name: Forgotten Keeper's Lantern
artifact.keeper_lantern.description: Place indoors or outdoors for a warm light.
artifact.keeper_lantern.lore: Before the forest had paths, a keeper lit this lantern for those returning home late. The glass still smells of pine resin.
artifact.herbalist_flask.name: Woodland Herbalist's Flask
artifact.herbalist_flask.description: Right-click while holding: restore 60 energy. Once per day.
artifact.herbalist_flask.lore: There is always a sip of cool herbal tea inside. The recipe on the stopper is faded, but a smiling leaf is still visible.
artifact.harvest_seal.name: Old Surveyor's Seal
artifact.harvest_seal.description: Right-click: gain 8 valley fragments. Once per day.
artifact.harvest_seal.lore: Touching soil with this seal reveals long-forgotten field boundaries, leading to traces of the valley's early settlements.
artifact.memory_musicbox.name: Music Box of Kind Memories
artifact.memory_musicbox.description: Right-click: restore 40 health. Once per day.
artifact.memory_musicbox.lore: The melody changes a little each time. It sounds like something a loved one once hummed while rain tapped at the window.
artifact.forest_heart.name: Heart of the First Forest
artifact.forest_heart.description: An ancient glowing relic. Place it in your home or on the farm.
artifact.forest_heart.lore: An amber droplet holds a leaf from a tree older than the first house in the valley. Even in winter, its light feels like summer.
artifact.brass_gear.name: Ancient Lift Gear
artifact.brass_gear.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.brass_gear.lore: A tiny rune marks every tooth. Dwarven mechanics seem to have numbered their parts to repair machines in total darkness.
artifact.rune_tablet.name: Apprentice Runecarver's Tablet
artifact.rune_tablet.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.rune_tablet.lore: The final line reads 'I will stop drawing a moustache on my teacher.' The earlier lines were carefully scraped away.
artifact.miner_goblet.name: Underhill Master's Goblet
artifact.miner_goblet.description: A table ornament and a research archive exhibit.
artifact.miner_goblet.lore: Heavy, yet perfectly balanced. Its rim reads: 'Good work begins after a good lunch.'
artifact.dwarf_thermos.name: Dwarven Thermos
artifact.dwarf_thermos.description: Right-click: receive a Triple Shot Espresso. Once per day.
artifact.dwarf_thermos.lore: The lid has three settings: 'hot', 'very hot', and 'break time is over'. Fortunately, the last setting is stuck.
artifact.resonant_lens.name: Resonant Lens
artifact.resonant_lens.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal an exact find. Once per day.
artifact.resonant_lens.lore: Through the glass, faint echoes of hammer strikes are visible. The lens reveals places once shaped by working hands.
artifact.clockwork_mole.name: Clockwork Digger
artifact.clockwork_mole.description: Right-click at a dig site: pinpoint a find. Once per day.
artifact.clockwork_mole.lore: This tiny brass animal stubbornly turns its nose toward buried antiquities. Its belly is engraved: 'Dig with curiosity.'
artifact.mountain_heart.name: Memory of the Deep Mountain
artifact.mountain_heart.description: Right-click: gain 8 dwarven fragments. Once per day.
artifact.mountain_heart.lore: This crystal remembers the shape of objects once placed beside it. Bridges and stairways of an underground city flicker in its depths.
artifact.clay_whistle.name: Sailor's Clay Whistle
artifact.clay_whistle.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.clay_whistle.lore: Shaped like a fish, perhaps a gift to a child before a long voyage. Fine white sand fills the opening.
artifact.sailor_buckle.name: Sunken Schooner Buckle
artifact.sailor_buckle.description: A collectible antiquity. Can be displayed on a table.
artifact.sailor_buckle.lore: Beneath the salt is an image of three stars. Gunther found a ship of the same name in the harbour records, without a return date.
artifact.shell_comb.name: Mother-of-Pearl Comb
artifact.shell_comb.description: A table ornament and a research archive exhibit.
artifact.shell_comb.lore: Every tooth follows the shell's curve. At dusk, the comb casts reflections resembling distant sails.
artifact.tide_compass.name: Tide Compass
artifact.tide_compass.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal an exact find. Once per day.
artifact.tide_compass.lore: The needle knows nothing of north. It seeks things someone once missed dearly. Sailors considered that more useful.
artifact.pearl_casket.name: Salt-Pearl Casket
artifact.pearl_casket.description: Right-click: receive 3 clams. Once per day.
artifact.pearl_casket.lore: A tiny wave can be heard inside. Every morning, gifts from a distant shore appear despite the lid being closed all night.
artifact.moon_shell.name: Moon-Tide Shell
artifact.moon_shell.description: Right-click: restore 60 energy. Once per day.
artifact.moon_shell.lore: Inside is the sea from no known map. Listening makes your breathing steady and lets weariness drift away.
artifact.abyss_beacon.name: Beacon of Forgotten Depths
artifact.abyss_beacon.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal an exact find. Once per day.
artifact.abyss_beacon.lore: This light guided travellers where the sun never shone. Its base bears a map of a coastline long since claimed by the sea.
artifact.rain_pitcher.name: Pitcher of the First Rain
artifact.rain_pitcher.description: Right-click: water up to 9 tilled tiles in front of you. Once per day; no charge is spent without dry soil.
artifact.rain_pitcher.lore: A tiny cloud was painted beneath the forest silt. Rain gathers in the pitcher every morning, though nobody has filled it for years.
artifact.storm_fork.name: Storm Tuning Fork
artifact.storm_fork.description: Right-click: reveal all dig-site finds within 8 tiles for 30 seconds. Once per day; hoe the highlighted tiles.
artifact.storm_fork.lore: Lightning exposed this instrument beneath charred roots. A quiet chord trembles between its prongs; underhill makers heard forgotten objects answer it.
artifact.past_lens.name: Lens of the Past
artifact.past_lens.description: Right-click: reveal a walkable trail of footprints to the nearest find and its old inscription for 30 seconds. Once a day; no trail preserves the charge.
artifact.past_lens.lore: The marks in its glass are tiny paths, not scratches. A dwarven maker engraved the rim: 'Things remember the way home, even when people forget.'
artifact.garden_flute.name: Forgotten Orchard Flute
artifact.garden_flute.description: Right-click near a fruit tree: grow one extra fruit, once every 7 game days. Requires a healthy mature tree in season, holding fewer than three fruits, within 5 tiles. Greenhouse season rules apply.
artifact.garden_flute.lore: A gardener played this flute while waiting for letters from distant lands. The trees grew used to her melody and still answer with a quiet rustle.
artifact.keeper_hourglass.name: Keeper's Hourglass
artifact.keeper_hourglass.description: Right-click at a dig location: report remaining finds and extend the nearest eligible site by one day. Once a day, once per site. Story caches cannot be extended.
artifact.keeper_hourglass.lore: The upper bulb never empties while someone carefully sorts their pottery shards. The keeper seems to have valued unfinished stories above timetables.
artifact.pocket_observatory.name: Pocket Observatory
artifact.pocket_observatory.description: Right-click outdoors after 8pm: forecast and open a two-find star expedition the next morning. Once a day; only one pending or active star expedition. Lasts 3 days from its first morning.
artifact.pocket_observatory.lore: Sailors carried it instead of heavy charts. Its needles point not north, but where tomorrow's light will first touch something long forgotten.
artifact.frozen_leaf.name: Sleeping Leaf Imprint
artifact.frozen_leaf.description: A rare find after the first snow. A golden leaf rests inside thin ice. Display it, donate it to Gunther's archive, or sell it.
artifact.frozen_leaf.lore: Someone scratched 'Until spring' on the back. They wanted to preserve their garden's last leaf, and winter kept the promise for them.
artifact.tide_calendar.name: Calendar of Four Tides
artifact.tide_calendar.description: A rare coastal find at the turn of a season. Four colored inlays mark the year's cycle. Display it, donate it to Gunther's archive, or sell it.
artifact.tide_calendar.lore: Sailors marked the first warm wind, the longest day, red leaves and still water before snow. This calendar, rather than the stars, told them when to come home.
artifact.star_glass.name: Star Glass
artifact.star_glass.description: An epic find in the soil beside a new meteorite on the farm. A cold light glimmers in dark glass. Display it, donate it to Gunther's archive, or sell it.
artifact.star_glass.lore: Dwarven makers called such shards 'windows without walls'. Gaze into its depths and a distant light seems to draw slowly closer.
artifact.reader_seal.name: Careful Reader's Seal
artifact.reader_seal.description: Right-click: +8 dwarven fragments once a day. A keepsake from Penny's story. All copies share one charge per player.
artifact.reader_seal.lore: Penny wrote 'try again' beside the dwarven mark. It now appears on every page that used to say 'wrong'.
artifact.garden_locket.name: First Garden Locket
artifact.garden_locket.description: Right-click: restore up to 60 energy once a day. A keepsake from Evelyn's story. Full energy preserves the charge.
artifact.garden_locket.lore: A pressed petal rests behind the glass. Evelyn says flowers grow better when you promise someone you'll show them in spring.
artifact.harbor_whistle.name: Quiet Harbour Whistle
artifact.harbor_whistle.description: Right-click at a dig site: reveal the nearest find once a day. A keepsake from Willy's story. No available find preserves the charge.
artifact.harbor_whistle.lore: Two short notes, one long. Willy says the signal means 'I'm here', which is sometimes all someone waiting ashore needs to hear.
